Pages read from Indeed on 2026-10-19, signed out, in a browser: no form was filled and nothing was applied to. Classes and inline styles are taken out (Indeed draws in React Native for the web, so its class names are generated and change; the adapter goes by `data-testid`s), and so are images, icons and tracking parameters; the job descriptions are cut to a few lines. The rest keeps the markup's nesting as drawn.

- **viewjob.html:** a job's own page, `https://www.indeed.com/viewjob?jk=5a2e49e6872d0c2b`, an Indeed Apply posting ("Apply now" to `smartapply.indeed.com`). The company links to its page on Indeed (`/cmp/…?fromjk=<the job's key>`), followed by its rating and the job's place. The page carries its schema.org `JobPosting` in JSON-LD (description cut short); the description in the page has a `<style>` inside it, as Indeed draws it.
- **search.html:** a search, `https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=software+engineer&l=San+Jose%2C+CA&vjk=d501d1fd236f6dc3`: three of the list's rows and the job open beside them. The open row is marked `vjs-highlight` and its link `aria-pressed="true"`; the third row is one the page lists at the key `abcdef0123456789`, which leads to no job. The open job's company has no page on Indeed: its name is plain text (`vj-company-name`), so the header names no key. A list has no JSON-LD.

Indeed Apply's own pages (`smartapply.indeed.com`) sit behind a sign-in and weren't read: the specs' step of it is made up.
